conditions: Serial execution; no local task tests, agents or other profilers ran concurrently.
Private user/network/PID namespaces and fresh configuration for every sample; no forced GC or profiler.
Dependency lock, automatic feature behavior, observer and exact Host are matched across Package variants.
Kernel page caches, CPU frequency and ambient machine activity were not controlled; two samples per variant/profile.
Ledger seed creation is outside the measured Host scope; resumed cold replay is included.
measurementBoundary: CPU and charged-memory counters cover the Host cgroup, including Workers and reaped children, through final observation before shutdown.
Observer, tmux, synthetic HTTP server and preparatory Ledger seed process are outside that cgroup.
Final RSS sums live process smaps_rollup readings; it is not aggregate peak process-tree RSS.
I/O counters belong to final surviving processes and omit exited children; they are not total process-tree I/O.
Charged-memory peak includes non-RSS charges and is not a cumulative allocation counter.
These runs do not measure allocations, GC, scheduler wakeups or largest main-thread tasks.
All individual gate breaches are retained, including the candidate background autocomplete-setup failure.

configDirectoryFollowup.candidateChange: Reuse public CONFIG_DIR_NAME in the shared Agents utility; source diff retained in evidence

tracedDeadlineFailure.diagnosis: The observer ended before the fixture final-response timer could fire; this run does not show a Provider deadlock. Earlier failures remain unattributed.

limits: Counts include Host threads, Workers and descendants through exit; observer, tmux, synthetic HTTP fixture and Ledger seeding are excluded.
Each variant has two fresh-profile observations in baseline/candidate/candidate/baseline order; shared runner activity and page cache are uncontrolled.
Traced elapsed times and feedback are diagnostics, not frozen-gate acceptance or causal stall attribution.
Foreground task births rise from 122 to 128 with the isolation implementation; identical requested work does not imply identical internal task counts. These costs remain included.
Background uses one Agent, unlike the two-Agent local CPU batch. Ledger task births are baseline61/61 and candidate60/61.
Evidence and raw trace contents remain hash-bound; only compact summaries were uploaded by CI. Automatic Naming is asserted by the unchanged observer but is not separately serialized in the summary.
All four runs used the fixed Pi 0.85.0 binary, 120x40 terminal, fresh private profiles and user/network/PID namespaces; no other task test, agent or profiler ran concurrently.
Profiler, render wrapper, FFI marks and strace were separate runs; their scheduling overhead is not bounded and their feedback is not acceptance evidence.
CPU sample stacks and gaps do not establish exact task duration or attribute the earlier unprofiled 48.868/72.710 ms failures.
The render diagnostic temporarily wrapped the native doRender method only in a private diagnostic extension, not in production code or a claimed public SDK contract.
All temporary observer and production instrumentation was removed; the observer restored to SHA-256 38e9965313e5608666b2399fc074456c94a06eaca6805d76a0803bfb8226f3a3.
No reduction of refresh cadence, eager prewarming, filesystem rewrite or native render change follows from these non-reproducing diagnostics.
